question.problem:
Solve the modular equation $5x≡12\,(\text{mod}\,44),$ expressing your answer as a nonnegative integer smaller than $44.$

*Hint: You may wish to use trial and error to find the appropriate multiplicative inverse.*

$x≡$
{{field-1}}$\,(\text{mod}\,44)$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that a linear congruence $ax≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n)$ has a unique solution modulo $n$ if and only if $\text{gcd}(a,n)=1.$

In the given congruence, we have $a=5$ and $n=44$, and

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(5,44)=1.
$$

So, our congruence does indeed have a unique solution.

To find the solution, we need to multiply both sides of the equation by the multiplicative inverse of $5\,(\text{mod}\,44).$ To find the inverse of $5\,(\text{mod}\,44)$, we compute the exponents of $5\,(\text{mod}\,44)$ until we get a result of $1\,(\text{mod}\,44):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{2} & ≡25 &  & (\text{mod}\,44) \\ {5}^{3} & ≡125≡37 &  & (\text{mod}\,44) \\ {5}^{4} & ≡37\cdot 5≡185≡9 &  & (\text{mod}\,44) \\ {5}^{5} & ≡9\cdot 5≡45≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,44)\end{aligned}
$$

So, $9\cdot 5≡1\,(\text{mod}\,44),$ which means that $9$ is the multiplicative inverse of $5$ (modulo $44$).

Now, multiplying both sides of our congruence by $9,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}5x & ≡12 &  & (\text{mod}\,44) \\ 9\cdot 5x & ≡9\cdot 12 &  & (\text{mod}\,44) \\ (9\cdot 5)x & ≡108 &  & (\text{mod}\,44) \\ 1\cdot x & ≡2\cdot 44+20 &  & (\text{mod}\,44) \\ x & ≡20 &  & (\text{mod}\,44)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x≡20\,(\text{mod}\,44).$
